note: Patches applied to a pinned sibling checkout before generation, so a module the compiler refuses to lower today can still ship. A patch here may only rewrite an expression into an equivalent the compiler does lower. It may NEVER change observable behavior -- absence, reference identity, equality, ordering, exception shape, task settlement -- because the generated header is then tested against the patched source, so a behavioral patch is a lie our own tests would certify. Each patch states the equivalence that makes it safe and the refusal it answers. The patch is applied after the pin integrity check and reverted when generation ends, so the checkout is only ever dirty inside one run. `baseCommit` pins the patch to the revision it was written against: a pin move that breaks the patch fails loudly instead of silently applying to different code.

patches.refusal: dual-sentinel optional property result requires one represented member value domain
patches.rewrite: Reads initializeNode's optional `obj` parameter through one non-optional local (`obj ?? {}`) instead of three optional chains.
patches.equivalence: PartialNode<T> declares every member optional, so `{}` inhabits Readonly<PartialNode<Node<Traits>>> and `obj ?? {}` yields an object whose every member read is undefined exactly when obj was undefined. `obj?.name ?? null` and `source.name ?? null` therefore agree on every input, as do the enabled and data reads. No member is written, no reference escapes, and the substituted object is unreachable after the call.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The refusal is in the emitter (cppCompilerBackend.ts:18888): an optional chain over a `T | null` member produces a dual-sentinel domain it cannot project. Member access on a non-optional binding is the one narrowing form it does lower. Flight could simply be written this way, so this patch is also the upstream suggestion.
patches.unblocks: node.ts stops being a root refusal. @flighthq/node, and the render/scene2d/scene3d tier behind it, remain blocked on the separate asserted-row refusal in hierarchy.ts.
patches.expires: when the emitter projects a dual-sentinel optional property result, or Flight adopts this form in its own source.

patches.refusal: could not convert 'flight::timeline::noop_construct_frame' from 'void()' to 'std::function<void(flight::StructuralRef<...Node2DTraits...>, double)>'
patches.rewrite: Gives noopConstructFrame the two parameters its target type declares, instead of none.
patches.equivalence: TimelineSource.constructFrame is declared `(target: Node2D, frame: number) => void`, and TypeScript admits a shorter parameter list for a longer one, which is why the zero-arity form type-checked. The body is empty, so the named parameters are never read and no call site changes -- the function's only use is as the right operand of `obj.constructFrame ?? noopConstructFrame`. Underscore names keep noUnusedParameters quiet.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: Parameter-count contravariance has no std::function equivalent: void() cannot construct std::function<void(A, B)>. The emitter would need to wrap the shorter function in an adapter that discards the extra arguments. Until it does, every TypeScript function assigned to a wider signature emits code that does not compile, and this is the instance that blocks @flighthq/timeline.
patches.unblocks: @flighthq/timeline's three headers compile. With this and statusbar deferred, every non-deferred fully-emitting package compiles together in one translation unit.
patches.expires: when the emitter adapts a narrower function to a wider std::function target, or Flight declares the parameters itself.

patches.refusal: Object.assign requires one closed callable-object target and an exact compatible object literal source
patches.rewrite: copyScreenInfo assigns ScreenInfo's 25 declared fields one by one instead of calling Object.assign with a computed source.
patches.equivalence: Object.assign copies own enumerable STRING keys, and for a Flight entity those are exactly the fields the interface declares -- ScreenInfo declares 25. The entity runtime lives under a symbol key, which Object.assign would not copy and which stripEntityRuntime deletes anyway, so neither path moves it. The explicit writes therefore produce the identical destination state, and they drop the intermediate object stripEntityRuntime allocated. stripEntityRuntime becomes unused in this module and its import is removed with it.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The emitter supports Object.assign only with a closed callable-object target and an object LITERAL source; here the source is a call result, so there is no literal to check against. Enumerating the fields removes the construct rather than asking the emitter to grow a case for it.
patches.unblocks: @flighthq/screen's single root refusal. Its other two refusals are pure cascade on this module, so the package should reach 3/3.
patches.expires: when the emitter accepts a non-literal Object.assign source. NOTE: this patch hard-codes ScreenInfo's field list, so a pin move that adds a field must re-derive it -- baseCommit forces that review.

patches.refusal: try/finally early return is retained as a return slot assignment followed by fallthrough
patches.rewrite: Expresses each circle contact test as an explicit if/else whose two branches each return, instead of an early miss return followed by the hit return.
patches.equivalence: Checked separately for circle-aabb, circle-circle, circle-obb, and circle-polygon: each lean test is called exactly once. When it succeeds, both forms immediately return writeCircleContact. When it fails, both forms clear the output manifold and immediately return false. In all four functions there is no statement between the original early return and hit return with an effect on the miss path; the same finally block releases the same acquired scratch object after either result.
patches.verification: Verified with the pinned compiler parsing and typing the patched source, independent compilation of the emitted header, and a public 2D sweep probe that failed against the unpatched header and passed after the patch (including the continuous circle hit at fraction 0.3). Flight's own package suite was not run because the disposable pinned Flight checkout has no installed workspace dependencies.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The pinned emitter flattens the early return inside try/finally into a return-slot assignment but then continues into and overwrites it with the later hit result. Explicit exhaustive branches give the lowering one return assignment per control-flow path.
patches.unblocks: Restores correct misses for the circle-aabb, circle-circle, circle-obb, and circle-polygon contact family and makes the continuous circle solver reachable through the public sweep after its discrete initial-overlap check misses.
patches.expires: when try/finally lowering preserves an early return before following statements, or Flight adopts the exhaustive branch form.

patches.refusal: narrowed intersection parameters emit Ref values with value-style member access
patches.rewrite: Types each private raycast helper with its named public shape interface instead of spelling the equivalent discriminated-union intersection.
patches.equivalence: The helpers read only members declared by CollisionBox3D, CollisionCapsule3D, CollisionCone3D, or CollisionCylinder3D and never read kind, mutate the object, retain it, or observe identity. Each switch arm has already narrowed the same object to that shape. Removing the redundant intersection and discriminant from the private parameter type therefore changes no accepted call or runtime operation.
patches.verification: Verified with the pinned compiler parsing and typing the patched source and independent compilation of the emitted raycast header, whose four helper parameters lower to structural rows and whose narrowed call sites use structural_ref_cast. Flight's own package suite was not run because the disposable pinned Flight checkout has no installed workspace dependencies.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The pinned emitter represents the anonymous intersection parameters as Ref<T> but emits every property access with '.', while named readonly interfaces lower through the supported structural-read path. This source form avoids changing a generated operator or carrying a copied override.
patches.unblocks: Makes raycast_collision_shape3_d.hpp compile and clears its _internal_index.hpp and contract.hpp cascades.
patches.expires: when property access on narrowed intersection parameters uses reference member access, or Flight adopts the named interface annotations.

patches.refusal: dual-sentinel optional property result requires one represented member value domain
patches.rewrite: Gives the private metadata helper one explicit nullable-property result shape, initializes the three consumers from their existing fallbacks, and replaces each value only when non-null metadata supplies it instead of combining optional chaining and nullish coalescing. It also makes the public glyph-index validity test explicit before reading the nullable array element.
patches.equivalence: The return annotation is exactly the structural union already inferred from the helper's two object literals. When metadata is null, both forms use fallback advances and metrics plus a new empty map. When metadata is present, both use its codepoint map; each nullable advances or metrics member replaces its fallback exactly when it is non-null. The helper returns a local plain object, so the rewrite neither changes accessor effects nor exposes the temporary empty map. For a numeric array index, JavaScript returns a stored outline only for a non-negative safe integer below length; the explicit guard rejects exactly every input for which the original indexed read produced undefined, including fractions, infinities, and out-of-range integers.
patches.whyNotUpstreamFirst: The pinned emitter first refuses an optional property read carrying both absent-object and nullable-member sentinels; merely spelling the fallbacks as branches then exposes that its inferred object-literal union stores null as a separate variant arm rather than an optional property. The explicit common result shape plus guarded reads express the same selection through supported storage and control flow. The index guard also prevents the now-emitted nullable array read from using unchecked Array::element for JavaScript property-access cases that should yield undefined. All forms remain suitable upstream TypeScript.
patches.unblocks: Emits readSwfFontGlyphOutlineSource instead of leaving a missing-function marker. The SWF headers still inherit separate shape package diagnostics and are remeasured after this patch rather than credited speculatively.
patches.expires: when the emitter represents dual-sentinel optional property results, or Flight adopts the explicit fallback form.
